checks: The uint-to-Nat-to-uint roundtrip is proved from the typed Fin bound, not an extra PC bound assumption.
At restricts the actual state PC to a checked site or exact EOF and binds actual code to the chosen Deposit/Exit runtime. The non-STOP hypothesis excludes EOF by the actual pinned decode-none fact.
The fixed-image decode equality is invoked only after deriving membership at the actual PC. No blanket arbitrary-bytecode decoder equality is introduced.
decode_some rules out referenceDecode = none using actual non-STOP, so it proves real source-decoder success rather than equality of two STOP defaults.
return_decode derives RETURN non-STOP and its none immediate from the actual decoded opcode; it requires neither a nonhalting-H premise nor a predicted instruction.
scope_limits: Applies only to the two fixed runtime images and states satisfying actual At.
Does not cover generic STOP/EOF agreement or arbitrary foreign bytecode; the truncated-PUSH mismatch remains outside scope.
Proves decoder binding, not RETURN execution, output, gas payment, or executable Python refinement.
